kindHint.PEC: Perfect electric conductor (E_tan = 0, counted in wall-loss Q). Unassigned outer faces default to PEC
kindHint.E-short: Electric symmetry wall (E_tan = 0, excluded from losses), e.g. the cut plane of a half model
kindHint.M-short: Magnetic symmetry wall / PMC (natural boundary), e.g. the cut plane of a half model
kindHint.port: Wave port face (PORT1, PORT2, …). Treated as a natural boundary in eigenmode analysis

analysis.findResonance: Find resonance after the sweep (1 port)

sparam.title: S-parameters
sparam.cutoff: {{name}}: estimated cutoff of the dominant mode fc ≈ {{fc}} GHz
sparam.unitaryHint: Below cutoff S is an amplitude ratio and |S11|²+|S21|²=1 does not hold. Phases of components below −60 dB are meaningless

sparam.estimateRejected: {{port}}: the estimate from S differs from the FEM solutions by up to {{dev}} %, so the solved points are connected instead

snapshots.title: Field snapshots
snapshots.hint: Solve the driven problem at one frequency (a_inc = 1 W incident) and show the field in 3D. Clicking the S plot fills in the frequency
snapshots.normalization: Displayed as Re(E e^{jφ}); normalized to a_inc = 1 (1 W incident in the propagating mode). Q0 = ωU/P0 is meaningful only near resonance

resonance.title: Resonance search
resonance.qe: External Qe = {{qe}} (peak height ω0U/4P_inc) / half-width {{width}} / S11 phase {{phase}}{{eig}}
resonance.q0: Internal Q0 = {{q0}} (σ = {{sigma}} S/m) / loaded QL = {{ql}} / coupling β = Q0/Qe = {{beta}}
resonance.noQ0: Internal Q0 omitted (no σ given; QL = Qe)
resonance.hint: The driven solution is refined around the U/P_inc maximum of the sweep. In a lossless model ωU/P_inc is four times the external Q, so Qe = ω0U/(4P_inc) is used
resonance.done:
Resonance search finished:
f0 = {{f0}} GHz, Qe = {{qe}}{{q0}}
resonance.q0NoWall: Internal Q0 = {{q0}} (dielectric loss only) / loaded QL = {{ql}} / coupling β = Q0/Qe = {{beta}}
resonance.q0Diel: Q0 breakdown: wall Q_wall = {{qWall}}, dielectric Q_diel = {{qDiel}} (1/Q0 = 1/Q_wall + 1/Q_diel)

bc.PEC: Make the selected curves PEC (perfect electric conductor wall)

ribbon.run: Confirm shape, materials and boundary conditions, then run solve (→ post) in a child process

physics.title: Physics (materials and boundaries)
physics.hint: Set the body (region) names, materials and the boundary conditions of faces. Both are written into the mesh, so decide them before meshing (changing them later remeshes at the analysis).
physics.overlapHint: Where bodies overlap, the smaller body wins (a dielectric body inside the vacuum body keeps its material). To make a separate body, choose the operation "New body" when creating the shape. You can also rename a body by double-clicking it in the browser.

regions.title: Regions and materials
regions.hint: Material per closed region (εr and tanδ accept expressions). Name and tag are written to the mesh. Click a row to highlight the region
regions.name: Name
regions.tagHint: Lowercase letters, digits and _ (normalized automatically; boundary names such as PEC are not allowed)
regions.none: No closed region (enclose an area with curves)

boundaries.title: Boundary conditions
boundaries.hint: Effective boundary condition and its source per curve. Without an explicit setting it is automatic (interfaces and the axis = None, otherwise PEC). Click a row to select the curve

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.hint: Settings are saved. Running auto-saves the project; results are kept as history (tree node Results)
analysis.targetHint: Sets the shift-invert shift to this frequency so modes near it are returned
analysis.animate: Add GIF animation for traveling waves
analysis.saveBeforeRun: Results are stored inside the project (data folder results\). Choose a project location first.
analysis.noResult: No result to post-process or report. Run an analysis first.
analysis.forceStopConfirm: Kill the child process? No result will be kept.

results.title: Results
results.noResult: No result to show. Pick one under Results in the tree, or open an h5 with 'Open result file…'

relation.geometry: Result from before the geometry was changed (differs from the current sketch)
relation.mesh: Result from before the mesh settings were changed
relation.settings: Result from before the analysis settings were changed

results.noPost: No post values (Q, R/Q …). Run 'Re-run post' on the Analysis tab
results.eWallHint: Draws the electric field (E_z, E_r) at PEC edge midpoints in red (TM0 only)
results.fieldHint: Double-click the plot to show the field at that point
results.gifNeedsTraveling: GIF animation is for traveling-wave results only (time phase 0→360°)

units.title: Change units
units.prompt:
Change the coordinate units from {{old}} to {{new}}. Convert the values too?
(points and dimensions with expressions are not converted)

view.axisRangePrompt: z min, z max, r min, r max (comma separated; empty = fit all)
view.axisRangeError: Enter four numbers separated by commas

run.title: Confirm analysis run
run.header: The analysis runs with the following settings. The project is auto-saved first.
run.targetAuto: from the lowest modes (no predicted frequency)
run.meshReuse: uses the mesh from the mesh tab ({{elements}} elements)
run.meshNew: the mesh is generated at the start of the run

hint.area: Samples the Z / R range on an nz × nr grid (units: m)
hint.line: Samples npts points on the line P1 → P2 (units: m)
hint.axis: Samples npts points on the symmetry axis r = 0 over the Z range (units: m)

fieldExport.powerHint: empty = no scaling. e.g. 1000 (1 kW wall loss)
fieldExport.instant: Write instantaneous (real) values for traveling wave (default: complex amplitude)

gif.title: Save GIF animation
gif.hint: Cycles the time phase 0→360° with the current display settings

view3d.title: 3D view
view3d.hint: The 2D field revolved about the z axis. Follows the shown result (n / phase / mode / time phase). Left drag rotates, right drag zooms, middle drag pans, F fits
view3d.unavailable: The 3D view needs pyvista and pyvistaqt: pip install -e .[viz3d]
view3d.noResult: No result to show (pick one on the Results tab)
view3d.eLineLevels: Number of contour levels (as the 2D E lines)
view3d.eLinesHint: Line spacing shows the field strength (TM0 only)
view3d.meridianHint: The 2D plot placed in 3D; with a revolution angle below 360° these are the cutaway faces
view3d.arrowNzHint: Grid divisions along z (same default as the 2D vectors' nz)
view3d.arrowNxyHint: Grid divisions along x and y (half of it along r on the meridian planes)

about.title: About AxiCavity-FEM
about.description: Resonant modes of axisymmetric cavities (TM0 and higher-order modes, standing and traveling waves) with the 2-D finite-element method.
about.licenseSource: The source code is MIT licensed. Dependencies (gmsh, PySide6 / Qt, …) keep their own licenses.
